note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Runny nose, nasal congestion, cough, and fever

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Young child with illness onset approximately 24 hours ago, beginning around supper time yesterday evening. Caregiver reports runny nose with clear nasal discharge and nasal congestion. Non-barky cough present. Patient pulling on ears and rubbing nose frequently. Rectal temperature measured at 100.3°F. Appetite variable - consumed approximately 7 ounces from bottle this morning, barely finished second bottle, refused cereal. Patient appears irritable and energetic but is fighting sleep. Sick contacts include older sister who is currently ill and playdate with nephew who has sinus infection.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Respiratory: Runny nose with clear nasal discharge, nasal congestion, non-barky cough
Ears: Ear pulling
Fever: Low-grade fever
Constitutional: Irritability, difficulty sleeping
Gastrointestinal: Decreased appetite
Skin: Cradle cap present and worsened

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Saline mist to nose, acetaminophen given this morning, baby Vick's applied to feet last night, humidifier in use

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Participates in playdates.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Respiratory: Lungs clear
Ears: Within normal limits
Skin: Cradle cap present and worsened

RESULTS
COVID-19: Negative

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Viral upper respiratory infection. Patient presenting with symptoms consistent with viral illness. Noted that sinus infections may originate as viral infection and potentially progress to bacterial if untreated; however, antibiotics not indicated at this time.

Plan:
1. Continue fluids and rest
2. Monitor closely for development of barky cough (concerning for croup); if barky cough develops, administer half teaspoon of prescribed medicine for five days
3. Zarbee's cough syrup for regular cough using pediatric under-1-year dosing if needed
4. Counseled on avoidance of honey in infants under 1 year of age due to botulism risk; agave is safe alternative
5. Cradle cap management: Use dandruff shampoo (Head & Shoulders, Selsun Blue, or Nizoral AD at regular strength) twice weekly, continue soft brush and baby oil for scale removal, avoid eye contact during rinsing; should improve within six weeks
6. Follow-up appointment in one week
7. Return to clinic if symptoms worsen
